claims.claim: All 50 forward passes and 300 Python runs were used.
claims.evidence: COUNTERS reports 300 Python runs and 50 charged forward passes; call 370 is charged pass 50.

claims.claim: The final submitted edit contains six tensors in /work/edited.
claims.evidence: SUBMITTED EDIT SET lists exactly the six reported tensors, with 14,155,175 entries changed; ledger 77–82 installs them.

claims.claim: The baseline contained 512 answers, with 460 token-cap failures and 52 correct non-failures.
claims.evidence: Call 4 reports 512 generations, 460 cut failures, accuracy 52/512, and no finished wrong or missing answers.

claims.claim: Baseline accuracy essentially equals the probability of termination.
claims.evidence: Call 4 shows every non-cut answer was correct; this holds when termination means avoiding the reported cut failure.

claims.claim: ' Wait' appeared about 338 times per failing trace versus 50 per successful trace.
claims.evidence: Ledger 42 explicitly records mean counts of 338 versus 50.

claims.claim: Boxes inside failing traces were correct 0/53 times.
claims.evidence: Call 61 establishes 0/53 for the last box, not for every box inside those traces.

claims.claim: The box before loop onset was correct 0/47 times.
claims.evidence: Call 61 reports box_before_onset n=47, mean correctness 0.000.

claims.claim: Top-1 next-token probability exceeded 0.9 at 99.2% of loop positions.
claims.evidence: Ledger 18–21 reports approximately 99%; the displayed output of call 47 does not expose the exact 99.2% statistic.

claims.claim: 89% of loop tokens copied a token 20–50 positions back.
claims.evidence: Ledger 18–21 records 89% copying; call 253 exposes notes specifying the approximately 20–50-token lag.

claims.claim: Loop periods were 30–50 tokens.
claims.evidence: Calls 107 and 123 identify particular periods, including 20, 23, 30 and 49; no displayed aggregate establishes the stated general range.

claims.claim: Gated DeltaNet memories decay in 2–6 tokens.
claims.evidence: Calls 55 and 281 show widely varying retention horizons, including much longer memories; call 281 reports retention as high as 0.9986 per step.

claims.claim: Attention was measured on two periodic traces, finding L7 head 5 mass 0.51 at lag 49 and 0.54 at lag 30, with recent mass 0.00–0.01.
claims.evidence: Call 122 collects attention for two traces; call 123 analyzes it; ledger 45 and 53 explicitly record these measurements.

claims.claim: Within-trace loop-minus-normal directions had split-half cosine 0.96–0.97 across 90 traces.
claims.evidence: Call 118 analyzes 90 loop traces; ledger 63–66 and 77–82 explicitly record the split-half cosine range.

claims.claim: The loop component grew by +0.43 over L14–16, +0.67 over L16–18 and +0.88 over L18–20.
claims.evidence: Ledger 77–82 explicitly records all three measured increments; calls 117 and 161 collect and analyze the relevant hidden states.

claims.claim: The loop component stabilized after those depth increments.
claims.evidence: The displayed measurements and ledger record growth but do not establish subsequent stabilization.

claims.claim: The six final projections used left multiplication by I minus lambda times the outer product of a measured unit loop direction.
claims.evidence: Ledger 63–66 and 77–82 describe direction removal, but the visible Python heads do not establish the exact formula for all six final tensors.

claims.claim: L16 linear_attn.out_proj used strength 0.30 and relative norm about 0.04.
claims.evidence: Ledger 77 confirms the tensor replacement, changing 2,097,086 entries, but its displayed reason omits strength and relative norm.

claims.claim: L18 linear_attn.out_proj used strength 0.30 and relative norm about 0.04.
claims.evidence: Ledger 78 confirms the tensor replacement, changing 2,097,097 entries, but its displayed reason omits strength and relative norm.

claims.claim: The final L20, L22 and L23 projection edits used strength 0.26.
claims.evidence: Ledger 63–66 specifies 0.26; final ledger 79–82 reinstalls the identical respective blobs.

claims.claim: The final L20 projection had relative norm 0.042.
claims.evidence: Call 77 reports relative norm 0.1677469 at strength 4.0 for the same direction; strength 0.26 implies approximately 0.0109, not 0.042.

claims.claim: Final relative norms were 0.040 for L22, 0.035 for L23 attention and 0.037 for L23 MLP.
claims.evidence: Ledger 80–82 identifies the final blobs and changed-entry counts but does not report these relative norms.

claims.claim: Final norm, embeddings and lm_head were untouched.
claims.evidence: The complete edit ledger contains no edits to these tensors; the submitted set contains only six layer projections.

claims.claim: No final tensor was scaled globally, and no final edit explicitly forced </think> or EOS.
claims.evidence: Ledger 77–82 installs direction-removal edits; earlier close-injection and head-scaling edits were reverted.

claims.claim: Measured loop excess at L20/L22/L23 was +0.789/+0.879/+0.674.
claims.evidence: Ledger 63–66 explicitly records the three excess measurements; call 115 displays the L20 measurement.

claims.claim: Strength 0.26 removed approximately 0.55/0.65/0.75 along the respective directions.
claims.evidence: Call 62 reports removed components 0.546, 0.649 and 0.747.

claims.claim: Good reasoning had component 1.27 versus a loop level of 2.84.
claims.evidence: The displayed outputs do not show this pair of values; calls 62 and 115 show other calibration values.

claims.claim: The late-only 0.26 edit produced +3.1 ± 2.0 points, with 17 rescues and 9 losses.
claims.evidence: Call 31 reports those results while the installed edit was the single L23 MLP projection at strength 0.75 (ledger 17; calls 29–30). The later 0.26 tests, calls 259 and 261, report zero and negative differences.

claims.claim: Strength 0.26 gave the only positive paired generation result.
claims.evidence: Call 241 reports +14.84 points for a close-injection edit; several later calls also report positive differences.

claims.claim: Strength 1.0 increased loop-tail </think> log-probability by 2.54 nats.
claims.evidence: Ledger 26–29 and 34–37 explicitly record the +2.54-nat screening measurement.

claims.claim: Strength 1.0 gave no accuracy gain.
claims.evidence: Ledger 34–37 installs strength 1.0; call 86 reports edited 10.16% versus original 12.5%, a negative difference.

claims.claim: Strength 4.0 produced 0% accuracy.
claims.evidence: Ledger 26–29 installs strength 4.0; call 81 reports 0/128 edited answers correct.

claims.claim: Strength 4.0 produced mid-sentence EOS.
claims.evidence: Calls 81, 109 and 110 establish widespread answerless endings, but the displayed excerpts do not establish the claimed EOS positions.

claims.claim: L23 neuron gates, dense LDA gates and a head-5 close write were tried.
claims.evidence: Ledger 47–61 records neuron-gated writes, ledger 71 records an LDA write, and ledger 73–75 records head-5 interventions.

claims.claim: All earlier close-injection designs failed because they fired at positions 1–2 of good traces and produced Here</think>.
claims.evidence: Ledger 61 and calls 221 and 227 support early-closing problems for particular gates; the log does not establish this exact position and failure mechanism for every design.

claims.claim: There were 18 paired validation runs totaling 4,224 paired answers.
claims.evidence: Calls 334, 335, 339, 340, 349, 350, 353, 355–357, 359, 362–366, 368 and 370 comprise 18 later validation runs totaling 4,480 pairs: seventeen runs of 256 and one of 128.

claims.claim: Those runs were independent and used held-out problems.
claims.evidence: Call 335 reuses the problem list from call 319; call 339 includes baseline problems such as gsm8k_train_7010 from call 4.

claims.claim: The frozen edit scored +0.09 ± 0.58 points, with 298 rescues and 294 losses.
claims.evidence: The 18 later validation calls listed above sum to 310 rescues and 329 losses over 4,480 pairs, yielding approximately -0.42 points.

claims.claim: The final pass scored edited 16.0% versus original 15.2%.
claims.evidence: Call 370 reports edited accuracy 0.16015625 and original accuracy 0.15234375.

claims.claim: Approximately 13–14% of paired answers flipped, about 7% rescued and 7% broken.
claims.evidence: The 18 later validation runs total 639 flips/4,480 pairs, approximately 14.3%, comprising 6.9% rescues and 7.3% losses.

claims.claim: Per-run differences included +3.9, +3.5, +2.3, -3.9, -2.7 and -2.7 points.
claims.evidence: Calls 357, 362 and 368 show the positive differences; calls 350, 353 and 355 show the negative differences.

claims.claim: Per-run noise was approximately 2.4 percentage points.
claims.evidence: Calls 357 and 362 report paired standard errors of 2.40 and 2.37 points; other later runs have similar errors.

claims.claim: The final pass had 214/256 edited traces hit the token cap.
claims.evidence: Call 370 reports 256 edited generations and cut_at_max_tokens=214.

claims.claim: Adding L16/L18 pulled performance down from a late-only +3.1-point result toward zero.
claims.evidence: Ledger 77–82 confirms adding L16/L18, but there is no controlled comparison establishing its effect; the attributed late-only +3.1 result actually belongs to ledger 17's single-tensor edit.

claims.claim: The Python budget was exhausted while L16/L18 remained installed.
claims.evidence: COUNTERS reports 300 Python runs; ledger 77–78 and the submitted set show L16/L18 remained, with no subsequent reverts.

claims.claim: An L7 head-5 ×0.5 screening test was attempted.
claims.evidence: Call 163 installs ×0.5 on 256 head-5 columns; call 164 runs edited teacher forcing; ledger 53 records the replacement.

claims.claim: That screening result was bitwise identical to its comparison pass.
claims.evidence: Call 166 reports fwd15 versus fwd17 max difference zero, with zero differing values out of 1,277,794.

claims.claim: A tooling fault made that test compare original weights against original weights, so the intended experiment never actually ran.
claims.evidence: Calls 166–167 show identical outputs despite a correctly saved head edit; they do not establish which weights were executed or prove a tooling fault.
